subject.title: typedocs-only PR to help others avoid kubernetes OOM-kills

question: Should OpenClaw's shared Kubernetes manifest ship a fixed `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1536` default, or keep that cap as optional operator guidance?
rationale: This is a public deployment default with upgrade/operator impact, and automation cannot choose the product policy for inherited Kubernetes manifests.

options.title: Require proof before defaulting
options.body: Correct the wording, add redacted Kubernetes proof, and only then accept the fixed default if the Kubernetes owner agrees it belongs in the shared manifest.

options.title: Make it optional guidance
options.body: Document the heap cap as an operator overlay or customization step so existing manifest consumers do not inherit a fixed runtime cap automatically.

options.title: Accept the fixed default deliberately
options.body: Maintainers may choose to ship the 1536 MiB cap now, owning the requirement that operators adjust it whenever they change the pod memory limit.

recommendation.title: Require proof before defaulting
recommendation.body: Correct the wording, add redacted Kubernetes proof, and only then accept the fixed default if the Kubernetes owner agrees it belongs in the shared manifest.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and have substantial history on the Kubernetes docs/manifests being changed.
